text:
Education in Nigeria is structured into primary, secondary, and tertiary levels, with the government mandating nine years of uninterrupted basic education under the Universal Basic Education (UBE) scheme. Primary education begins at age 5 and covers six years, culminating in a Common Entrance Examination (CECE) for admission to secondary schools. The secondary system follows a 6-3-3-4 model, consisting of three years of Junior Secondary School (JSS) and three years of Senior Secondary School (SSS), with students taking the West African Senior School Certificate Examination (SSCE) or General Certificate of Education (GCE) upon completion. Tertiary education includes universities, polytechnics, monotechnics, and colleges of education, which are largely public institutions but include a growing number of private universities. Admission to universities typically requires SSCE credits and a minimum JAMB score of 180, though direct entry is available for holders of National Certificate of Education or National Diploma.
The Nigerian education system is characterized by significant disparities between federal, state, and private institutions. Federal government schools are highly competitive, merit-based, and well-funded, often viewed as elite, whereas state-sponsored schools face challenges such as understaffing, irregular salary payments, and budget constraints, leading to a reliance on unqualified teachers. Private schools, particularly international and religious institutions, operate on a fee basis with rising costs and offer better facilities and curricula. Informal education and literacy programs, supported by NGOs and government initiatives, have been crucial in addressing illiteracy, though challenges remain regarding funding, regional inequalities (particularly in the North), security issues affecting rural areas, and the quality of vocational training. Recent developments include the approval of numerous new private universities and ongoing efforts to improve digital literacy and address gender disparities.
